records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶֽל־יַעֲקֹ֔ב ק֛וּם עֲלֵ֥ה בֵֽית־אֵ֖ל וְשֶׁב־שָׁ֑ם וַעֲשֵׂה־שָׁ֣ם מִזְבֵּ֔חַ לָאֵל֙ הַנִּרְאֶ֣ה אֵלֶ֔יךָ בְּבָרְחֲךָ֔מִפְּנֵ֖י עֵשָׂ֥ו אָחִֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: And said God to Jacob, arise, go up [to] Bethel and dwell there, and make there an altar to the God who appeared to you when you fled from before Esau your brother.
pieces: Then God said to Jacob, "Up, and go to Bethel, and make your home there. Build an altar there to the God who appeared to you as you fled from your brother Esau."

L.1: And God said to Jacob, "Arise, go up to Bethel and dwell there, and make an altar there to the God who appeared to you when you fled from Esau your brother."

R.1: God told Jacob, "Get ready and go up to Bethel. Live there, and build an altar to the God who appeared to you when you were running away from your brother Esau."

decisions.choice: Bethel, the God who appeared to you: the vow comes due
decisions.reason: At Bethel Jacob saw the stairway and vowed that if God brought him back safely, the LORD would be his God and the stone would become God's house (28:10-22). God now calls him back to keep that vow.

decisions.choice: go up: Bethel lies higher than Shechem
decisions.reason: Bethel is in the hill country, higher than Shechem. "Going up" is also the usual phrase for going to a place of worship.

decisions.choice: the God who appeared to you: God speaks of himself in the third person
decisions.reason: God refers to himself as "the God (El) who appeared to you", pointing Jacob back to the earlier meeting rather than simply saying "me".

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יַעֲקֹב֙ אֶל־בֵּית֔וֹ וְאֶ֖ל כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר עִמּ֑וֹ הָסִ֜רוּ אֶת־אֱלֹהֵ֤י הַנֵּכָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּתֹכְכֶ֔ם וְהִֽטַּהֲר֔וּ וְהַחֲלִ֖יפוּ שִׂמְלֹתֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And said Jacob to his household and to all who [were] with him, remove the gods of foreignness which [are] among you, and purify yourselves and change your clothes.
pieces: So Jacob told his family and everyone with him, "Get rid of every foreign god you have among you. Make yourselves clean and put on fresh clothes.

L.2: And Jacob said to his household and to all who [were] with him, "Put away the foreign gods that [are] among you, and purify yourselves and change your clothes.

R.2: So Jacob spoke to his family and to everyone traveling with him. "Throw away all the statues of other gods that you have," he said. "Wash yourselves and put on clean clothes.

decisions.choice: the foreign gods among you: idols carried by the household
decisions.reason: The household included Rachel, who had taken her father's household gods (31:19, 34), and probably the captives taken at Shechem (34:29). Before meeting God at Bethel the family must belong to him alone, as Joshua later demanded of Israel at Shechem (Joshua 24:14, 23).

decisions.choice: purify yourselves and change your clothes: making ready to meet God
decisions.reason: Washing and changing clothes prepared people to come before God; Israel did so before Sinai (Exodus 19:10, 14).

decisions.choice: statues of other gods
decisions.reason: Readable says what the gods were: images that could be handed over and buried (verse 4).

records.source: וְנָק֥וּמָה וְנַעֲלֶ֖ה בֵּֽית־אֵ֑ל וְאֶֽעֱשֶׂה־שָּׁ֣ם מִזְבֵּ֗חַ לָאֵ֞ל הָעֹנֶ֤ה אֹתִי֙ בְּי֣וֹם צָֽרָתִ֔י וַיְהִי֙ עִמָּדִ֔י בַּדֶּ֖רֶךְ אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָלָֽכְתִּי׃
records.gloss: And let us arise and let us go up [to] Bethel, and I will make there an altar to the God who answered me in [the] day of my distress, and he has been with me on the way which I have gone.
pieces: Then let us set out and go up to Bethel. I will make an altar there to the God who answered me when I was in trouble and has stayed with me on every road I have traveled."

L.3: And let us arise and go up to Bethel, and I will make an altar there to the God who answered me in the day of my distress and has been with me on the way I have gone."

R.3: Then let us go up to Bethel. There I will build an altar to the God who answered me when I was in great trouble. God has been with me everywhere I have gone."

decisions.choice: the day of my distress: Jacob's flight from Esau
decisions.reason: Jacob fled with nothing but his staff (32:11), and in fear of Esau prayed for rescue (32:12). God had promised at Bethel, "I am with you and will keep you wherever you go" (28:15); Jacob now says that God kept it.

records.source: וַיִּתְּנ֣וּ אֶֽל־יַעֲקֹ֗ב אֵ֣ת כָּל־אֱלֹהֵ֤י הַנֵּכָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּיָדָ֔ם וְאֶת־הַנְּזָמִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּאָזְנֵיהֶ֑ם וַיִּטְמֹ֤ן אֹתָם֙ יַעֲקֹ֔ב תַּ֥חַת הָאֵלָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר עִם־שְׁכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And they gave to Jacob all the gods of foreignness which [were] in their hand and the rings which [were] in their ears, and hid them Jacob under the terebinth which [was] near Shechem.
pieces: They handed over to Jacob all the foreign gods they had, along with the rings from their ears, and Jacob buried them under the great tree near Shechem.

L.4: And they gave Jacob all the foreign gods that [were] in their hands and the rings that [were] in their ears, and Jacob hid them under the terebinth that [was] near Shechem.

R.4: So they gave Jacob all the statues of other gods. They also gave him the rings they wore in their ears. Jacob buried all of them under the big oak tree near Shechem.

decisions.choice: the rings in their ears: jewelry linked with the worship of other gods
decisions.reason: Earrings could serve as amulets or bear the marks of gods. Gold earrings were later melted down to make the golden calf (Exodus 32:2-4).

decisions.choice: the terebinth: a great tree, a landmark at Shechem
decisions.reason: The 'elah is a large, long-lived tree, the terebinth or an oak. Abraham camped by the great tree of Moreh at Shechem (12:6), and Joshua later set up a stone under the oak there (Joshua 24:26).

decisions.choice: buried
decisions.reason: The verb taman means to hide by burying (Joshua 7:21). Balanced and Readable say "buried"; Literal keeps "hid".

records.source: וַיִּסָּ֑עוּ וַיְהִ֣י׀חִתַּ֣ת אֱלֹהִ֗ים עַל־הֶֽעָרִים֙ אֲשֶׁר֙ סְבִיבֹ֣תֵיהֶ֔ם וְלֹ֣א רָֽדְפ֔וּ אַחֲרֵ֖י בְּנֵ֥י יַעֲקֹֽב׃
records.gloss: And they set out, and there was [the] terror of God on the cities which [were] around them, and they did not pursue after the sons of Jacob.
pieces: As they moved on, a dread sent by God came over the towns around them, and no one went after Jacob's sons.

L.5: And they set out, and a terror from God was on the cities around them, and they did not pursue the sons of Jacob.

R.5: Then they left. God made the people in all the nearby towns very afraid, so no one chased after Jacob's sons.

decisions.choice: terror of God: a fear God sent on the people
decisions.reason: The phrase may mean a fear that God sent, or simply a very great fear. Jacob had feared the peoples of the land would attack (34:30); God protects the family in spite of what Simeon and Levi had done. The same holy fear goes before Israel in Exodus 23:27.

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֨א יַעֲקֹ֜ב ל֗וּזָה אֲשֶׁר֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ כְּנַ֔עַן הִ֖וא בֵּֽית־אֵ֑ל ה֖וּא וְכָל־הָעָ֥ם אֲשֶׁר־עִמּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And came Jacob to Luz, which [is] in [the] land of Canaan, that [is] Bethel, he and all the people who [were] with him.
pieces: Jacob arrived at Luz in the land of Canaan, the place now known as Bethel, together with all the people in his company.

L.6: And Jacob came to Luz, which [is] in the land of Canaan, that [is], Bethel, he and all the people who [were] with him.

R.6: Jacob and all his people came to Luz in the land of Canaan. Luz is also called Bethel.

decisions.choice: Luz, that is, Bethel: the town's old name and its new one
decisions.reason: The town was called Luz; Jacob named the place Bethel, "house of God", after his dream there (28:19).

records.source: וַיִּ֤בֶן שָׁם֙ מִזְבֵּ֔חַ וַיִּקְרָא֙ לַמָּק֔וֹם אֵ֖ל בֵּֽית־אֵ֑ל כִּ֣י שָׁ֗ם נִגְל֤וּ אֵלָיו֙ הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים בְּבָרְח֖וֹ מִפְּנֵ֥י אָחִֽיו׃
records.gloss: And he built there an altar and called the place El-Bethel, for there had revealed themselves to him God when he fled from before his brother.
pieces: There he built an altar and named the place El-Bethel, "God of Bethel", because it was there God had shown {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} to him as he was fleeing from his brother.

L.7: And he built an altar there and called the place El-Bethel, because there God had revealed {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} to him when he fled from his brother.

R.7: Jacob built an altar there. He called the place El-Bethel, which means "the God of Bethel." He chose this name because God had shown {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} to Jacob there when he was running away from his brother.

decisions.choice: El-Bethel: the God of Bethel
decisions.reason: Jacob names the place after the God he met there, not only the place itself (31:13, "I am the God of Bethel").

decisions.choice: God had revealed himself: the verb is plural
alternatives: the divine beings had revealed themselves
decisions.reason: Elohim, "God", is plural in form, and here the verb is plural too, as sometimes happens (20:13). The sense is God, the one who appeared; the plural may also recall the angels Jacob saw going up and down (28:12).

decisions.choice: God had revealed himself
decisions.reason: The verb is plural, but its subject is the one God (m2), so every level uses the singular "himself".

records.source: וַתָּ֤מָת דְּבֹרָה֙ מֵינֶ֣קֶת רִבְקָ֔ה וַתִּקָּבֵ֛ר מִתַּ֥חַת לְבֵֽית־אֵ֖ל תַּ֣חַת הָֽאַלּ֑וֹן וַיִּקְרָ֥א שְׁמ֖וֹ אַלּ֥וֹן בָּכֽוּת׃פ
records.gloss: And died Deborah, [the] nurse of Rebekah, and she was buried below Bethel under the oak; and he called its name Allon-bacuth.
pieces: Deborah, who had nursed Rebekah, died there and was buried beneath the oak below Bethel. So the tree came to be called Allon-bacuth, "Oak of Weeping".

L.8: And Deborah, Rebekah's nurse, died, and she was buried below Bethel under the oak; and its name was called Allon-bacuth.

R.8: Rebekah's old nurse Deborah died. They buried her under the oak tree below Bethel. So that tree was named Allon-bacuth, which means "Oak of Weeping."

decisions.choice: Deborah, Rebekah's nurse: a lifelong servant of the family
decisions.reason: A nurse went with Rebekah when she left home to marry Isaac (24:59); only here is she named. Her death is mourned as a loss to the whole family. Rebekah's own death is never told.

decisions.choice: Allon-bacuth: oak of weeping
decisions.reason: Allon means oak and bakhut weeping. The name keeps the memory of the mourning for her.

decisions.choice: its name was called
decisions.reason: The verb has no named subject: someone, or people in general, gave the name. Literal and Balanced use the passive.

records.source: וַיֵּרָ֨א אֱלֹהִ֤ים אֶֽל־יַעֲקֹב֙ ע֔וֹד בְּבֹא֖וֹ מִפַּדַּ֣ן אֲרָ֑ם וַיְבָ֖רֶךְ אֹתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And appeared God to Jacob again when he came from Paddan-aram, and he blessed him.
pieces: Now that Jacob had come back from Paddan-aram, God appeared to him once more and blessed him.

L.9: And God appeared to Jacob again when he came from Paddan-aram, and blessed him.

R.9: God appeared to Jacob a second time, now that he was back from Paddan-aram, and God blessed him.

decisions.choice: again: a second appearance at Bethel
decisions.reason: God first appeared to Jacob here as he left the land (28:13-15). Now he appears again on Jacob's return, closing the circle of the journey.

records.source: וַיֹּֽאמֶר־ל֥וֹ אֱלֹהִ֖ים שִׁמְךָ֣ יַעֲקֹ֑ב לֹֽא־יִקָּרֵא֩ שִׁמְךָ֨ע֜וֹד יַעֲקֹ֗ב כִּ֤י אִם־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ יִהְיֶ֣ה שְׁמֶ֔ךָ וַיִּקְרָ֥א אֶת־שְׁמ֖וֹ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And said to him God, your name [is] Jacob; not will be called your name again Jacob, but Israel will be your name. And he called his name Israel.
pieces: God said to him, "Your name is Jacob, but from now on that will not be your name. Your name will be Israel." So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave him the name Israel.

L.10: And God said to him, "Your name [is] Jacob; your name will no longer be called Jacob, but Israel will be your name." And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} called his name Israel.

R.10: God said to him, "Your name is Jacob. But people will not call you Jacob anymore. From now on your name is Israel." So God named him Israel.

decisions.choice: Israel will be your name: the name given at the Jabbok confirmed
decisions.reason: The man who wrestled with Jacob gave him this name (32:29). God now confirms it at Bethel, as God renamed Abram and Sarai when making the covenant (17:5, 15). Israel probably means "God strives" or "he strives with God".

decisions.choice: God (for "he")
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who gave the name; Literal and Balanced keep the pronoun.

records.source: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ ל֨וֹ אֱלֹהִ֜ים אֲנִ֨י אֵ֤ל שַׁדַּי֙ פְּרֵ֣ה וּרְבֵ֔ה גּ֛וֹי וּקְהַ֥ל גּוֹיִ֖ם יִהְיֶ֣ה מִמֶּ֑ךָּ וּמְלָכִ֖ים מֵחֲלָצֶ֥יךָ יֵצֵֽאוּ׃
records.gloss: And said to him God, I [am] God Almighty; be fruitful and multiply; a nation and a company of nations will be from you, and kings from your loins will come out.
pieces: God also said to him, "I am God Almighty. Be fruitful and grow in number. A nation, a whole assembly of nations, will come from you, and kings will be born from your line.

L.11: And God said to him, "I [am] God Almighty: be fruitful and multiply. A nation and an assembly of nations will come from you, and kings will come out of your body.

R.11: God also said to him, "I am God Almighty. Have many children, and let your family grow. Your family will become a nation, and many nations. Kings will come from your family.

decisions.choice: God Almighty: El Shaddai
decisions.reason: The name with which God made the covenant with Abraham (17:1) and with which Isaac blessed Jacob (28:3). Its exact meaning is uncertain; the ancient translations took it as "the Almighty".

decisions.choice: be fruitful and multiply ... kings: the blessing of creation and of Abraham
decisions.reason: The command of 1:28 and 9:1 and the promise of nations and kings to Abraham (17:6) are now given to Jacob. Isaac had prayed for the same "assembly of peoples" (28:3).

decisions.choice: from your loins: from your own body, your descendants
decisions.reason: The loins are the seat of a man's power to father children.

records.source: וְאֶת־הָאָ֗רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָתַ֛תִּי לְאַבְרָהָ֥ם וּלְיִצְחָ֖ק לְךָ֣ אֶתְּנֶ֑נָּה וּֽלְזַרְעֲךָ֥ אַחֲרֶ֖יךָ אֶתֵּ֥ן אֶת־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: And the land which I gave to Abraham and to Isaac, to you I will give it, and to your offspring after you I will give the land.
pieces: The land that I gave to Abraham and to Isaac is yours; I give it to you, and to your descendants after you I will give the land."

L.12: And the land that I gave to Abraham and to Isaac I will give to you, and to your offspring after you I will give the land."

R.12: I gave this land to Abraham and Isaac. Now I will give it to you and to your descendants after you."

decisions.choice: I will give the land: the promise passed to the third generation
decisions.reason: The gift of the land runs through the promises to Abraham (12:7; 13:15; 17:8) and Isaac (26:3). Jacob now receives it in full, back in the land after his years away.

records.source: וַיַּ֥עַל מֵעָלָ֖יו אֱלֹהִ֑ים בַּמָּק֖וֹם אֲשֶׁר־דִּבֶּ֥ר אִתּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And went up from him God at the place where he had spoken with him.
pieces: And God rose and left him there, at the place where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had been speaking with him.

L.13: And God went up from him at the place where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had spoken with him.

R.13: Then God left Jacob and went up from the place where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had talked with him.

decisions.choice: God went up from him: the end of the appearance
decisions.reason: The same words close God's appearance to Abraham in 17:22.

records.source: וַיַּצֵּ֨ב יַעֲקֹ֜ב מַצֵּבָ֗ה בַּמָּק֛וֹם אֲשֶׁר־דִּבֶּ֥ר אִתּ֖וֹ מַצֶּ֣בֶת אָ֑בֶן וַיַּסֵּ֤ךְ עָלֶ֨יהָ֙ נֶ֔סֶךְ וַיִּצֹ֥ק עָלֶ֖יהָ שָֽׁמֶן׃
records.gloss: And set up Jacob a pillar at the place where he had spoken with him, a pillar of stone, and he poured on it a drink offering and poured on it oil.
pieces: There, where God had spoken with him, Jacob raised a standing stone, and he poured a drink offering over it and oil as well.

L.14: And Jacob set up a pillar at the place where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had spoken with him, a pillar of stone, and he poured a drink offering on it and poured oil on it.

R.14: Jacob set up a large stone as a marker in the place where God had talked to him. He poured wine on it as an offering, and he poured olive oil on it too.

decisions.choice: a pillar: a standing stone marking a holy place
decisions.reason: Jacob had set up and anointed a stone at Bethel before (28:18). Standing stones marked places where something important had happened; later, pillars at the shrines of other gods were forbidden (Deuteronomy 16:22).

decisions.choice: a drink offering: wine poured out to God
decisions.reason: This is the first drink offering in Scripture. In later worship, wine was poured out alongside the sacrifices (Numbers 15:5-10).

decisions.choice: God (for "he")
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name God to make clear who spoke. Literal keeps the pronoun, with the deity pronoun span.

records.source: וַיִּקְרָ֨א יַעֲקֹ֜ב אֶת־שֵׁ֣ם הַמָּק֗וֹם אֲשֶׁר֩ דִּבֶּ֨ר אִתּ֥וֹ שָׁ֛ם אֱלֹהִ֖ים בֵּֽית־אֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And called Jacob the name of the place where had spoken with him there God, Bethel.
pieces: And the place where God had spoken with him, Jacob called Bethel.

L.15: And Jacob called the name of the place where God had spoken with him Bethel.

R.15: Jacob named the place where God had talked with him Bethel, which means "house of God."

decisions.choice: Bethel: the name given again
decisions.reason: Jacob had named the place Bethel, "house of God", on his outward journey (28:19). Naming it again on his return seals what God has done in between.

records.source: וַיִּסְעוּ֙ מִבֵּ֣ית אֵ֔ל וַֽיְהִי־ע֥וֹד כִּבְרַת־הָאָ֖רֶץ לָב֣וֹא אֶפְרָ֑תָה וַתֵּ֥לֶד רָחֵ֖ל וַתְּקַ֥שׁ בְּלִדְתָּֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And they set out from Bethel, and there was yet a stretch of the land to come to Ephrath, and gave birth Rachel, and she had hard labor in her giving birth.
pieces: They moved on from Bethel, and while there was still a stretch of road left before Ephrath, Rachel's time came, and her labor was very hard.

L.16: And they set out from Bethel, and there was still some distance to go to Ephrath, and Rachel went into labor, and she had hard labor in giving birth.

R.16: Then they left Bethel. On the way, before they reached Ephrath, Rachel began to give birth. It was a very hard birth.

decisions.choice: a stretch of the land: some distance
decisions.reason: Kivrat ha'arets is an unknown measure of distance, probably a short one (48:7; 2 Kings 5:19).

decisions.choice: Ephrath: the district of Bethlehem
decisions.reason: Ephrath is the older name of the area of Bethlehem (verse 19; Ruth 4:11; Micah 5:2).

records.source: וַיְהִ֥י בְהַקְשֹׁתָ֖הּ בְּלִדְתָּ֑הּ וַתֹּ֨אמֶר לָ֤הּ הַמְיַלֶּ֨דֶת֙ אַל־תִּ֣ירְאִ֔י כִּֽי־גַם־זֶ֥ה לָ֖ךְ בֵּֽן׃
records.gloss: And it was, when she had hard labor in her giving birth, said to her the midwife, do not fear, for also this [one is] for you a son.
pieces: When her labor was at its worst, the midwife told her, "Do not be afraid; this one is a son for you too."

L.17: And while she was in hard labor in giving birth, the midwife said to her, "Do not be afraid, for this one too [is] a son for you."

R.17: While she was struggling to give birth, the woman helping her said, "Do not be afraid. You have another boy!"

decisions.choice: this one too is a son for you: Rachel's prayer answered
decisions.reason: When Joseph was born, Rachel named him with the prayer "May the LORD add to me another son" (30:24). The midwife tells her the prayer has been answered, even as she dies.

decisions.choice: the woman helping her
decisions.reason: Readable explains the word for a reader who may not know it.

records.source: וַיְהִ֞י בְּצֵ֤את נַפְשָׁהּ֙ כִּ֣י מֵ֔תָה וַתִּקְרָ֥א שְׁמ֖וֹ בֶּן־אוֹנִ֑י וְאָבִ֖יו קָֽרָא־ל֥וֹ בִנְיָמִֽין׃
records.gloss: And it was, when went out her soul, for she died, and she called his name Ben-oni; and his father called him Benjamin.
pieces: As her life was slipping away, for she was dying, she called him Ben-oni, "son of my sorrow". His father, though, called him Benjamin, "son of the right hand".

L.18: And as her soul was departing, for she was dying, she called his name Ben-oni; but his father called him Benjamin.

R.18: Rachel was dying. With her last breath she named her son Ben-oni, which means "son of my sorrow." But his father named him Benjamin, which means "son of the right hand."

decisions.choice: as her soul was departing: as she breathed her last
decisions.reason: Nefesh is the life or breath; its going out is death.

decisions.choice: Ben-oni: son of my sorrow
decisions.reason: 'Oni can mean trouble or sorrow, which fits Rachel's dying; the same letters can also mean strength or vigor (49:3, of Reuben). The dying mother most likely names her pain.

decisions.choice: Benjamin: son of the right hand
decisions.reason: The right hand stands for strength, favor and good fortune. Since the right is south for one facing east, the name may also mean "son of the south": he is the only son of Jacob born in Canaan, south of Paddan-aram.

records.source: וַתָּ֖מָת רָחֵ֑ל וַתִּקָּבֵר֙ בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ אֶפְרָ֔תָה הִ֖וא בֵּ֥ית לָֽחֶם׃
records.gloss: And died Rachel and was buried on [the] way to Ephrath, that [is] Bethlehem.
pieces: Rachel died and was laid to rest beside the road to Ephrath, that is, Bethlehem.

L.19: So Rachel died and was buried on the way to Ephrath, that [is], Bethlehem.

R.19: So Rachel died. She was buried beside the road to Ephrath, the town now called Bethlehem.

decisions.choice: Ephrath, that is, Bethlehem: Rachel's grave on the way
decisions.reason: Rachel was buried by the road, not in the family tomb at Machpelah. Jeremiah 31:15 pictures Rachel weeping for her children at Ramah, and Matthew 2:18 applies the verse to the children of Bethlehem.

records.source: וַיַּצֵּ֧ב יַעֲקֹ֛ב מַצֵּבָ֖ה עַל־קְבֻרָתָ֑הּ הִ֛וא מַצֶּ֥בֶת קְבֻֽרַת־רָחֵ֖ל עַד־הַיּֽוֹם׃
records.gloss: And set up Jacob a pillar over her grave; it [is the] pillar of [the] grave of Rachel until this day.
pieces: Jacob raised a standing stone over her grave; it is the stone of Rachel's grave, and it stands there to this day.

L.20: And Jacob set up a pillar over her grave; it [is] the pillar of Rachel's grave to this day.

R.20: Jacob set up a large stone on her grave. It is still there today, showing where Rachel is buried.

decisions.choice: to this day: still standing when the account was written
decisions.reason: The phrase tells the first readers that the marker could still be seen. Rachel's tomb is mentioned again as a landmark in 1 Samuel 10:2.

records.source: וַיִּסַּ֖ע יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיֵּ֣ט אָֽהֳלֹ֔המֵהָ֖לְאָה לְמִגְדַּל־עֵֽדֶר׃
records.gloss: And set out Israel and pitched his tent beyond Migdal-eder.
pieces: Israel traveled on and pitched his tent on the far side of Migdal-eder.

L.21: And Israel set out and pitched his tent beyond Migdal-eder.

R.21: Israel moved on and set up his tent past Migdal-eder, which means "tower of the flock."

decisions.choice: Israel: the narrator now uses the new name
decisions.reason: From here on Jacob is often called Israel in the story, though not always; both names are used down to the end of the book.

decisions.choice: Migdal-eder: tower of the flock
decisions.reason: A watchtower for shepherds, somewhere between Bethlehem and Hebron. Micah 4:8 uses the name for Jerusalem as a shepherd's tower.

records.source: וַיְהִ֗י בִּשְׁכֹּ֤ן יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בָּאָ֣רֶץ הַהִ֔וא וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ רְאוּבֵ֔ן וַיִּשְׁכַּב֙אֶת־בִּלְהָה֙פִּילֶ֣גֶשׁ אָבִ֔יווַיִּשְׁמַ֖ע יִשְׂרָאֵ֑לוַיִּֽהְי֥וּ בְנֵֽי־יַעֲקֹ֖ב שְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָֽׂר׃
records.gloss: And it was, when dwelt Israel in that land, and went Reuben and lay with Bilhah, [the] concubine of his father; and heard Israel. And were the sons of Jacob twelve.
pieces: During Israel's stay in that land, Reuben went and lay with Bilhah, his father's concubine, and word of it reached Israel. There were twelve sons of Jacob.

L.22: And while Israel dwelt in that land, Reuben went and lay with Bilhah his father's concubine; and Israel heard [of it]. Now the sons of Jacob were twelve.

R.22: While Israel was living there, his son Reuben had sex with Bilhah, one of his father's wives. Israel found out about it. Jacob had twelve sons.

decisions.choice: lay with Bilhah his father's concubine: a claim to his father's place
decisions.reason: To take a ruler's or father's concubine was a bid for his authority (2 Samuel 16:21-22; 1 Kings 2:22). Bilhah was Rachel's slave woman and mother of Dan and Naphtali (30:3-8). For this Reuben lost the firstborn's rights (49:3-4; 1 Chronicles 5:1).

decisions.choice: and Israel heard of it: the Hebrew stops here
alternatives: and Israel heard, and it was evil in his sight
decisions.reason: The Masoretic text marks a paragraph break in the middle of this verse, after "Israel heard", as if the silence were deliberate. The Greek translation adds "and it seemed evil to him". The Hebrew text is followed here.

decisions.choice: concubine: a wife of lower rank
decisions.reason: A pilegesh was a secondary wife, often a former slave, without the full rights of a principal wife. Bilhah is called both Jacob's wife (30:4) and his concubine.

decisions.choice: one of his father's wives
decisions.reason: Readable avoids the unfamiliar word "concubine"; Bilhah is also called Jacob's wife in 30:4.

records.source: בְּנֵ֣י לֵאָ֔ה בְּכ֥וֹר יַעֲקֹ֖ב רְאוּבֵ֑ן וְשִׁמְעוֹן֙ וְלֵוִ֣י וִֽיהוּדָ֔ה וְיִשָּׂשכָ֖ר וּזְבוּלֻֽן׃
records.gloss: [The] sons of Leah: [the] firstborn of Jacob, Reuben, and Simeon and Levi and Judah and Issachar and Zebulun.
pieces: Leah's sons were Reuben, Jacob's firstborn, then Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar and Zebulun.

L.23: The sons of Leah: Reuben, Jacob's firstborn, and Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar and Zebulun.

R.23: Leah's sons were Reuben, who was Jacob's oldest son, and Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar and Zebulun.

decisions.choice: the sons of Leah: the twelve listed by their mothers
decisions.reason: The list groups the sons by mother: Leah's six, Rachel's two, and two each for the slave wives Bilhah and Zilpah. Reuben is still named firstborn, right after the wrong of verse 22.

records.source: בְּנֵ֣י רָחֵ֔ל יוֹסֵ֖ף וּבִנְיָמִֽן׃
records.gloss: [The] sons of Rachel: Joseph and Benjamin.
pieces: Rachel's sons were Joseph and Benjamin.

L.24: The sons of Rachel: Joseph and Benjamin.

R.24: Rachel's sons were Joseph and Benjamin.

records.source: וּבְנֵ֤י בִלְהָה֙ שִׁפְחַ֣ת רָחֵ֔ל דָּ֖ן וְנַפְתָּלִֽי׃
records.gloss: And [the] sons of Bilhah, [the] slave woman of Rachel: Dan and Naphtali.
pieces: The sons of Bilhah, Rachel's servant, were Dan and Naphtali.

L.25: And the sons of Bilhah, Rachel's slave woman: Dan and Naphtali.

R.25: The sons of Bilhah, Rachel's servant, were Dan and Naphtali.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable (style guide); Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: וּבְנֵ֥י זִלְפָּ֛ה שִׁפְחַ֥ת לֵאָ֖ה גָּ֣ד וְאָשֵׁ֑ר אֵ֚לֶּה בְּנֵ֣י יַעֲקֹ֔ב אֲשֶׁ֥ר יֻלַּד־ל֖וֹ בְּפַדַּ֥ן אֲרָֽם׃
records.gloss: And [the] sons of Zilpah, [the] slave woman of Leah: Gad and Asher. These [are the] sons of Jacob who were born to him in Paddan-aram.
pieces: The sons of Zilpah, Leah's servant, were Gad and Asher. These were Jacob's sons, born to him in Paddan-aram.

L.26: And the sons of Zilpah, Leah's slave woman: Gad and Asher. These [are] the sons of Jacob who were born to him in Paddan-aram.

R.26: The sons of Zilpah, Leah's servant, were Gad and Asher. These were Jacob's sons. They were born in Paddan-aram.

decisions.choice: born to him in Paddan-aram: a summary of the whole list
decisions.reason: The closing line sums up the twelve as a group. Benjamin, the one exception, has just been born in Canaan (verses 16-18); the summary speaks of the family as a whole.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable (style guide); Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֤א יַעֲקֹב֙ אֶל־יִצְחָ֣ק אָבִ֔יו מַמְרֵ֖א קִרְיַ֣ת הָֽאַרְבַּ֑ע הִ֣וא חֶבְר֔וֹן אֲשֶׁר־גָּֽר־שָׁ֥ם אַבְרָהָ֖ם וְיִצְחָֽק׃
records.gloss: And came Jacob to Isaac his father [at] Mamre, Kiriath-arba, that [is] Hebron, where had sojourned Abraham and Isaac.
pieces: Jacob finally reached his father Isaac at Mamre, by Kiriath-arba (that is, Hebron), where first Abraham and then Isaac had lived as foreigners.

L.27: And Jacob came to Isaac his father at Mamre, at Kiriath-arba, that [is], Hebron, where Abraham and Isaac had sojourned.

R.27: At last Jacob reached his father Isaac's home at Mamre, near the town of Kiriath-arba, now called Hebron. Abraham and Isaac had both lived there as foreigners.

decisions.choice: Mamre, Kiriath-arba, that is, Hebron: Abraham's old home
decisions.reason: Mamre was where Abraham settled and built an altar (13:18), and where he bought the burial cave (23:2, 19). Kiriath-arba ("town of Arba") was the older name of Hebron (Joshua 14:15).

decisions.choice: sojourned: lived as resident foreigners
decisions.reason: Abraham and Isaac lived in the land as outsiders who did not own it, except for the grave they had bought (23:4).

records.source: וַיִּֽהְי֖וּ יְמֵ֣י יִצְחָ֑ק מְאַ֥ת שָׁנָ֖ה וּשְׁמֹנִ֥ים שָׁנָֽה׃
records.gloss: And were the days of Isaac one hundred years and eighty years.
pieces: Isaac lived to the age of 180.

L.28: And the days of Isaac were 180 years.

R.28: Isaac lived to be 180 years old.

records.source: וַיִּגְוַ֨ע יִצְחָ֤ק וַיָּ֨מָת֙ וַיֵּאָ֣סֶף אֶל־עַמָּ֔יו זָקֵ֖ן וּשְׂבַ֣ע יָמִ֑ים וַיִּקְבְּר֣וּ אֹת֔וֹ עֵשָׂ֥ו וְיַעֲקֹ֖ב בָּנָֽיו׃פ
records.gloss: And breathed his last Isaac and died and was gathered to his people, old and satisfied of days; and buried him Esau and Jacob his sons.
pieces: Isaac's breath failed, and he died and was gathered to his people, an old man who had his fill of years. His sons Esau and Jacob laid him in the grave.

L.29: And Isaac breathed his last and died, and was gathered to his people, old and full of days; and Esau and Jacob his sons buried him.

R.29: Then Isaac died. He was very old and had lived a long, full life. He joined his family members who had died before him. His sons Esau and Jacob buried him.

decisions.choice: was gathered to his people: joined his ancestors in death
decisions.reason: The phrase is used of Abraham (25:8) and Ishmael (25:17). It speaks of death as joining those who went before, not only of burial.

decisions.choice: old and full of days: satisfied with a long life
decisions.reason: Said also of Abraham (25:8). Isaac's death is told here, though he may have lived on into the years of the Joseph story; Genesis closes one family's account before beginning the next.

decisions.choice: Esau and Jacob his sons buried him: the brothers together at the grave
decisions.reason: As Isaac and Ishmael buried Abraham (25:9), so the two rival brothers bury their father together, in the cave of Machpelah (49:31). Esau is named first, as the older son.
